newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon sees powerhouse in Hughes deal.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon sees powerhouse in Hughes deal.

text.p: Raytheon Co chairman and chief executive Dennis Picard said his company's deal to acquire General Motors Corp's Hughes Aircraft defense operations will create a powerhouse.
"We are truly creating another defense electronics powerhouse," Picard said in a statement announcing the deal.

The company, which will carry the Raytheon name, will have revenues of $21 billion on a proforma basis. Over $13 billion of that will be in defense electronics, Raytheon said. It said the current backlog of the combined entity will be about $23 billion, with defense electronics accounting for $18 billion.

Raytheon said the deal, coupled with its recently announced acquisition of Texas Instruments Inc's defense business, will result in a slight dilution to the earnings of the combined company in 1997, compared to earnings of Raytheon on a stand-alone basis for the same period, it said.
The transaction will be minimally accretive in 1998 and increasingly accretive thereafter, it said. It expects the deal to close by mid-year, it added.

Picard said the strategic combination of Raytheon and the defense businesses of Texas Instruments and Hughes "enables us to address changes head-on" due to the end of the Cold War "and to grow in the best segment of the defense business."

C. Michael Armstrong, chairman and chief executive of Hughes Electronics Corp which operates Hughes Aircraft, said Raytheon and Hughes "will create a much more competitive company that can better serve the defense market with leadership in systems and electronics."
According to the statement, John Weaver, president of Hughes Aircraft will report to Picard as president of Raytheon Hughes Systems, which will operate as a division of the combined company.

Armstrong, Charles Noski, currently vice chairman and chief financial officer of Hughes Electronics, and an independent director of GM to be named later will become board members of the combined company.
